article.story: MOBILE, Ala. -- — Keenan Phillips scored a 7-yard rushing touchdown with 1:46 left, Jayvon Henderson intercepted a pass in the end zone in the closing seconds and South Alabama beat Appalachian State 20-13 on Friday in the regular-season finale for both teams. South Alabama’s Cam Robinson picked off a pass in the end zone early in the fourth quarter and on App State’s next possession Jaquari Lewis was stopped for no gain on a fourth-and-inches run with 5:44 left to preserve a 13-all tie before Phillips capped an 11-play, 73-yard drive with the go-ahead touchdown. Bishop Davenport was 15-of-25 passing for 211 yards with a touchdown and an interception to go with 40 yards rushing on six carries for South Alabama (7-5, 5-3 Sun Belt Conference). James London, who kicked a 42-yard field goal in the second quarter, made a 29-yarder with about 6:49 remaining in the third that gave the Mountaineers a 13-10 lead. Lewis finished with 93 yards rushing and a TD on 23 carries for App State (7-5, 5-3). Malachi Singleton was 22-of-28 passing for 240 yards with two interceptions. Davenport threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Everett Hunter that opened the scoring about 7 minutes into the game and Dylan Freebury kicked a 21-yard field goal with 2:46 left in the first quarter that gave the Jaguars a 10-0 lead. The Mountaineers fell to 5-1 when they rush for at least 100 yards and 6-2 in one-score games this season. Up next App State: Awaits a likely bowl bid.
